361462.title: Malnegro–Ozeki's $\hat{A}$-coloring conjecture for line graphs of cubic graphs
361462.statement: Let $G$ be a 2-edge-connected simple cubic graph with an even number of edges. Its **line graph** $L(G)$ has one vertex for each edge of $G$, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding edges of $G$ are incident. Let $\hat{A}$ be the graph obtained by adding two pendant edges to two different vertices of a triangle and then adding two edges between the degree-two vertex and the two adjacent degree-three vertices. An $H$-coloring of a graph is a pair of total functions $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ and $g:V(G)\to V(H)$ such that $f$ is a proper edge-coloring and, for every vertex $u$, $f(\partial_G(u))=\partial_H(g(u))$. **Malnegro–Ozeki's conjecture.** The line graph $L(G)$ admits an $\hat{A}$-coloring. The paper presents this as an analogue for future research after disproving the corresponding $\bar{X}$-coloring conjecture; no resolution is given here.

361774.title: Matroid-rooted bounded regular packing conjecture for mixed hyperarborescences
361774.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}=(V,\mathcal{E}\cup\mathcal{A})$ be a mixed hypergraph, let $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}$, let $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}^{V}$, let $S$ be a multiset of vertices in $V$, and let $M=(S,r_M)$ be a matroid. For $U,W\subseteq V$, write $S_U$ for the elements of $S$ rooted in $U$, and let $g_k$ denote the function used in the bounded-packing conditions. A subpartition $\mathcal{P}$ of $W$ is a family of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets of $W$.

**Matroid-rooted bounded regular packing conjecture.** There exists an $M$-rooted $(f,g)$-bounded $k$-regular packing of mixed hyperarborescences in $\mathcal{F}$ if and only if the conditions and hold and, for all $U,W\subseteq V$ and every subpartition $\mathcal{P}$ of $W$,

$$
e_{\mathcal{E}\cup\mathcal{A}}(\mathcal{P})+r_M(S_U)+g_k(W-U)\geq k|\mathcal{P}|+f(U-W).
$$

This conjecture seeks the mixed-hypergraph analogue of the established characterization for mixed graphs. The source identifies it as an open problem; it would follow from the proposed orientation extension in the second conjecture.

366524.title: The set-system intersection bound modulo prime powers
366524.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $q=p^\alpha$, with $\alpha\geq 1$. Let $k\geq 2$ be an integer, let $L\subseteq \{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$ be a proper subset with size $s>0$, and let $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a set system. Assume that $|F|\notin L\pmod q$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$, while $|F_1\cap\cdots\cap F_k|\in L\pmod q$ for every collection of $k$ distinct sets from $\mathcal F$. Suppose that there exist $t\leq q-1$ integers $k_1,\ldots,k_t\in\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$ such that $|F|\pmod q\in\{k_1,\ldots,k_t\}$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. **The set-system intersection bound modulo prime powers.** Under these hypotheses,

$$
|\mathcal F|\leq (k-1)\sum_{j=q-t}^{q-1}{n\choose j}.
$$

The conjecture is proposed as a strengthening of the paper's Theorem 3; the stated bound would extend the linear-algebra method to set systems whose member sizes occupy at most $t$ residue classes modulo $q$, with all $k$-wise intersections restricted to $L$.

366801.title: Gartland's breakability conjecture for wall-subdivision-free graphs
366801.statement:
For a positive integer $t$, let $\mathcal{L}_t$ denote the graph class used in the source. A graph is **$k$-breakable** if, for every weight function $w\colon V(G)\to[0,1]$, it has a $w$-balanced separator with a core of size strictly less than $k$. A $w$-balanced separator is a set whose removal leaves every component with weight at most $1/2$, and a core for a set $Y$ is a set $X$ such that $Y\subseteq N[X]$. A subdivision of the $t\times t$-wall is obtained by subdividing edges of that wall.

**Gartland's conjecture.** For every positive integer $t$, there is an integer $d=d(t)$ such that every $\mathcal{L}_t$-free graph $G$ with no induced subgraph isomorphic to a subdivision of the $t\times t$-wall is $d$-breakable.

The conjecture concerns induced-subgraph obstructions to small tree independence number and is presented as support for a broader program involving walls and domination-based separators. The source states that its theorem on $\mathcal{M}_t^*$-free graphs provides evidence, but does not specify a resolution.

366921.title: The converse characterization of unique minimal \mathcal{X}-matroids
366921.statement: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a collection of subsets defining the class of $\mathcal{X}$-matroids, and suppose that this class is nonempty. Let $v_{\mathcal{X}}$ be the function constructed from the sequence $(\operatorname{val}_{\mathcal{X}}^{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$. A set function is **submodular** if it satisfies $v_{\mathcal{X}}(A)+v_{\mathcal{X}}(B)\geq v_{\mathcal{X}}(A\cup B)+v_{\mathcal{X}}(A\cap B)$ for all subsets $A,B$. **Converse characterization conjecture.** The function $v_{\mathcal{X}}$ is submodular if and only if there exists a unique minimal $\mathcal{X}$-matroid. This would complete the characterization begun by the preceding lemma, which proves that submodularity of $v_{\mathcal{X}}$ implies that $v_{\mathcal{X}}$ is the rank function of the unique minimal $\mathcal{X}$-matroid; the converse is left conjectural in the source.

367922.title: Uniformization conjecture for combinatorial Ricci flow
367922.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be an infinite disk triangulation with intersection angles $\Phi\in [0,\frac{\pi}{2}]^E$. Its **$1$-skeleton** is the graph formed by its vertices and edges, and a graph is **VEL-hyperbolic** when it has the corresponding vertex extremal-length property. A **locally finite univalent circle packing** of $\mathcal{T}$ in the unit disc is a circle packing whose contact graph is $\mathcal{T}$ and whose circles are locally finite and univalent.

**Uniformization of the CRF.** The following statements are equivalent: the combinatorial Ricci flow on $\mathcal{T}$ converges for every initial value in hyperbolic background geometry; there exists a locally finite univalent circle packing of $\mathcal{T}$ in the unit disc; and the $1$-skeleton of $\mathcal{T}$ is VEL-hyperbolic.

The conjecture extends the equivalence between convergence of combinatorial Ricci flow, existence of a hyperbolic circle-packing metric, and VEL-hyperbolicity from the finite setting to infinite disk triangulations. The source notes that the second and third conditions are equivalent by He’s theorem and that convergence implies the existence of a hyperbolic circle-packing metric; the implication from VEL-hyperbolicity to convergence remains to be proved.

368286.title: Archer et al.'s enumeration conjectures for cyclic permutation pattern avoidance
368286.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a cyclic permutation in $S_n$, written in one-line notation as $\pi_1\pi_2\cdots\pi_n$ and in cycle form as $(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n)$. The **standard cycle form** is the cyclic rotation beginning with $1$. Let $\mathcal{A}_n(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k;\tau)$ be the set of cyclic permutations in $S_n$ that avoid each pattern in $\{\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k\}$ in one-line form and avoid $\tau$ in standard cycle form, and write

$$
a_n(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k;\tau)=|\mathcal{A}_n(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k;\tau)|.
$$

**Archer et al.'s conjectures.** For the indicated values of $n$, the following enumerations hold:

$$
a_n(3421,4321;213)=F_{2n-3}\quad\text{for every integer }n\geq2,
$$

where $F_n$ is the $n$-th Fibonacci number, and

$$
a_n(1324,1423;213)=\binom{n}{3}+1\quad\text{for every positive integer }n\geq3.
$$

These conjectures concern simultaneous pattern avoidance in the one-line and standard cycle forms of cyclic permutations. The source presents them as proposed further directions for research, and no resolution is supplied here.

369838.title: Adams et al.'s cyclic sieving conjecture for Statistic 373
369838.statement:
A permutation statistic is a map from permutations to nonnegative integers, and two statistics are **equidistributed** when they have the same value-distribution on permutations. The **Corteel involution** is the involution on permutations described in the paper, and the cyclic sieving phenomenon concerns the fixed-point counts of powers of an involution.

**Adams et al.'s conjecture.** The number of weak excedances that are also mid-points of a decreasing subsequence of length $3$ (Statistic $373$ in FindStat) is equidistributed with the cycle descent number (Statistic $317$ in FindStat), and thus exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon under involutions with $1$ point for $n=0$ and $2^{n-1}$ points for all $n\geq 1$. In particular, this statistic exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon with respect to the Corteel involution.

This conjecture concerns an instance of cyclic sieving for permutation statistics and is presented as the conjecture proved in the paper. Its relationship with the Corteel involution places it in the paper's broader program of constructing cyclic sieving phenomena using continued-fraction methods.

370345.title: The asc-last and des-first equidistribution conjecture for Jacobi and André permutations
370345.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{J}_{n}$ be the set of Jacobi permutations and $\mathfrak{A}_{n}$ the set of André permutations. For a permutation $\pi$, let $\operatorname{asc}(\pi)$, $\operatorname{des}(\pi)$, $\operatorname{last}(\pi)$, and $\operatorname{first}(\pi)$ denote its numbers of ascents and descents and its last and first letters, respectively. Define

$$
j_{n,i,k}^{(\operatorname{asc},\operatorname{last})}=\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft|\{\,\pi\in\mathfrak{J}_{n}:\operatorname{asc}(\pi)=i\text{ and }\operatorname{last}(\pi)=k\,\}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright|
$$

and

$$
a_{n,i,k}^{(\operatorname{des},\operatorname{first})}=\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft|\{\,\pi\in\mathfrak{A}_{n}:\operatorname{des}(\pi)=i\text{ and }\operatorname{first}(\pi)=k\,\}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright|.
$$

**The asc-last and des-first equidistribution conjecture.** For all $n\geq1$, $i\geq0$, and $k\geq1$, we have

$$
j_{n,i,k}^{(\operatorname{asc},\operatorname{last})}=a_{n,i,k}^{(\operatorname{des},\operatorname{first})}.
$$

The conjecture would refine the separately known equidistributions of ascents with descents and of the last letter with the first letter between these two permutation classes.

371018.title: Leader–Russell–Walters' transitive-set conjecture for Euclidean Ramsey sets
371018.statement: A finite set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is **Ramsey** if, for every $k$, there exists an integer $n$ such that every $k$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ contains a monochromatic isometric copy of $X$. A finite set is **transitive** if a group acts transitively on it; a set is isometric to a subset of a finite transitive set when some finite transitive Euclidean set contains an isometric copy of it. **Leader–Russell–Walters' conjecture.** A set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is Ramsey if and only if it is isometric to a subset of a finite transitive set. This conjecture is presented as a rival to Graham's conjecture and concerns whether the known Ramsey constructions account for all Ramsey sets. The paper investigates the converse relationship with subsolubility and reports that only two possible exceptions remain among nearly all known examples.

371084.title: Sun's perfect-power repulsion conjecture for the partition function
371084.statement:
Let $p(n)$ denote the number of unrestricted integer partitions of $n$, with $p(0)=1$. An integer is a **perfect power** if it has the form $m^k$ with integers $m\ge 2$ and $k\ge2$. For fixed $k\ge2$, define the distance from $p(n)$ to the nearest $k$th power by

$$
\Delta_k(n):=\min_{m\ge0}|p(n)-m^k|.
$$

**Sun's perfect-power repulsion conjecture.** The partition function $p(n)$ repels perfect powers in the following senses: (i) for every $n\ge2$ and $k\ge2$, $p(n)\neq m^k$ for all integers $m\ge2$; and (ii) for every $k\ge2$ and $d\ge0$, only finitely many $n$ satisfy $\Delta_k(n)\le d$.

The first assertion is Sun's original no-perfect-powers conjecture, while the second is the stronger perfect-power repulsion conjecture developed with later generalizations by Merca et al. The paper supports these conjectures through analogous finiteness results for restricted partition functions $p_B(n)$, rather than proving the stated claims for $p(n)$ itself.

371680.title: The acyclic hero characterization for tournaments
371680.statement:
Let $T$ and $H$ be tournaments. A tournament is an **acyclic hero** if there is a constant $c_H$ such that every $H$-free tournament has acyclic dichromatic number at most $c_H$. For tournaments $H_1,H_2$, let $H_1\Rightarrow H_2$ denote the tournament formed from disjoint copies by orienting every arc from $H_1$ to $H_2$, and let $\Delta(H_1,H_2,H_3)$ denote the cyclic composition of three tournaments. Write $k$ for the transitive tournament $TT_k$. For every $k$, define

$$
H_k=TT_k\Rightarrow(\Delta(k,1,1)\Rightarrow TT_k),
$$

and let $\mathcal{AH}$ be the class of tournaments that occur as subtournaments of some $H_k$.

**The acyclic hero conjecture.** A tournament $H$ is an acyclic hero if and only if $H\in\mathcal{AH}$.

The forward implication is proved in the paper, as are several examples of tournaments in $\mathcal{AH}$ that are acyclic heroes. The converse, and hence the characterization, remains open.

375248.title: The product-beating conjecture for non-degenerate genus-one systems
375248.statement:
Let $L=(L_1,\ldots,L_t)$ be a non-degenerate genus-one translation-invariant system of equations over $\mathbb{F}_q$, where each $L_j$ is a translation-invariant equation in $s$ variables. A set $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ is **$L$-free** if the only simultaneous solutions of $L_j(x_1,\ldots,x_s)=0$ for $1\leq j\leq t$ in $A$ are diagonal solutions with $x_1=\cdots=x_s$. The system has genus one when there is no nonempty proper subset $I\subsetneq [s]$ such that $\sum_{i\in I}c_{i,j}=0$ for every $1\leq j\leq t$, where $L_j(x_1,\ldots,x_s)=\sum_{i=1}^s c_{i,j}x_i$. **The product-beating conjecture.** If $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ is $L$-free and has size $c^n$, then there exists an $L$-free set $B\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^m$ for some $m>n$ such that

$$
|B|>c^m.
$$

This would extend the corresponding product-beating result from a single translation-invariant equation to systems of equations; the non-degeneracy assumption is necessary because a degenerate system makes the whole space $L$-free. The claim is presented as an expectation for systems and no resolution is supplied here.

375631.title: Finiteness of the single-theater misère quotient
375631.statement:
Let the single-theater game have escalation set $S=\{1,\dots,m\}$. Its **misère quotient** is the commutative monoid obtained by identifying positions that are interchangeable in every disjunctive sum, with outcomes recorded by the subset of classes that are losing for the mover. **Finiteness conjecture.** For every $m$, the misère quotient of the single-theater game is finite. Consequently, multi-theater misère stability is decidable from the image of the joint state in this finite commutative monoid.

The single-theater misère game itself is solved exactly: its $\mathcal{P}$-positions are those with $r\equiv 1\pmod{m+1}$. The conjecture would provide a finite algebraic invariant for deciding multi-theater outcomes, extending the role of Grundy values in normal play; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

375763.title: Balogh–Linz–Patkós' odd-parity conjecture for intersecting k-Sperner families
375763.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $2^{[n]}$ denote the Boolean lattice, and let a family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be **$t$-intersecting** if $|A\cap B|\ge t$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{F}$, and **$k$-Sperner** if it contains no chain of length $k+1$. When $n+t$ is odd, set

$$
q=\frac{n+t-1}{2}.
$$

For a fixed $t$-set $T\subseteq[n]$, define the $q$-uniform $t$-star and its upper shadow by

$$
\mathcal{S}_T=\left\{S\in\binom{[n]}{q}:T\subseteq S\right\},
$$

$$
\nabla_s(\mathcal{F})=\left\{A\in\binom{[n]}{s}:\text{ there exists }F\in\mathcal{F}\text{ with }F\subseteq A\right\}
$$

for $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{r}$ and $s\ge r$, and let

$$
\mathcal{B}_T(t,k)=\mathcal{S}_T\cup\bigcup_{i=1}^{k-1}\binom{[n]}{q+i}\cup\left(\binom{[n]}{q+k}\setminus\nabla_{q+k}(\mathcal{S}_T)\right).
$$

Its size is

$$
|\mathcal{B}_T(t,k)|=\binom{n-t}{q-t}+\sum_{i=1}^{k}\binom{n}{q+i}-\binom{n-t}{q+k-t}.
$$

**Balogh–Linz–Patkós' conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $n_0=n_0(k,t)$ such that if $n+t$ is odd, $n>n_0$, and $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is a $t$-intersecting $k$-Sperner family, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\le\binom{n-t}{q-t}+\sum_{i=1}^{k}\binom{n}{q+i}-\binom{n-t}{q+k-t}.
$$

This is the odd-parity counterpart of the even-parity extremal problem, with the fixed-star construction providing the predicted sharp bound. The source presents it as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied there.

375948.title: Jollivet–Sharafutdinov inverse Steklov spectral conjecture
375948.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a smooth surface with boundary $M=\partial\Omega$, and let $g_1$ and $g_2$ be Riemannian metrics on $\Omega$. Two metrics are **$\sigma$-isometric** when there exist a diffeomorphism $\Phi:\Omega\to\Omega$ and a function $\rho\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}_+)$ such that $\rho|_M=1$ and

$$
g_2=\rho\Phi^*g_1.
$$

**Jollivet–Sharafutdinov inverse Steklov spectral conjecture.** The metrics $g_1$ and $g_2$ have the same Steklov spectrum if and only if they are $\sigma$-isometric. This conjecture identifies the natural obstruction to recovering a surface metric from its Steklov spectrum: boundary-fixing conformal changes preserve the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, while the conjecture asserts that these changes and diffeomorphisms account for all isospectrality. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

376343.title: Kiraly–Tanigawa's body-pin rigidity characterization conjecture
376343.statement:
Let $H=(W,E)$ be a multigraph, and let $G_H$ be the body-pin graph obtained by replacing each $w\in W$ with a body and identifying distinct pairs of body vertices according to the edges of $H$. For disjoint subsets $X,Y\subseteq W$, let $d_H(X,Y)$ be the number of edges between them and define

$$
\ell_H(X,Y)=
\begin{cases}
6 & \text{if }d_H(X,Y)\geq 3,\\
5 & \text{if }d_H(X,Y)=2,\\
3 & \text{if }d_H(X,Y)=1,\\
0 & \text{if }d_H(X,Y)=0.
\end{cases}
$$

**Kiraly–Tanigawa's body-pin conjecture.** The graph $G_H$ is rigid in $\mathbb{R}^3$ if and only if, for every partition $\mathcal{P}=\{P_1,P_2,\dots,P_t\}$ of $W$,

$$
\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq t}\ell_H(P_i,P_j)\geq 6(|\mathcal{P}|-1).
$$

This is a conjectured characterization of rigidity for body-pin graphs in three dimensions. The source attributes it to Kiraly and Tanigawa and does not report a resolution.

382375.title: Cyclic difference matrix conjecture for the Fibonacci-like partition construction
382375.statement:
Let $q_{i,j}=q_{i,j}^{[m,n]}$ be the non-negative integers obtained in Algorithm; these integers are independent of $m$ and $n$. For each $i\geq 1$, consider the sequence $\{q_{i,j}\}_{j\in\mathbb Z^{\geq 0}}$. **Cyclic difference matrix conjecture.** For every $i\geq 1$, the sequence $\{q_{i,j}\}_{j\in\mathbb Z^{\geq 0}}$ is a permutation of $\mathbb Z^{\geq 0}$, and for every pair of natural numbers $i_1<i_2$, every integer appears exactly once in the sequence

$$
\{q_{i_1,j}-q_{i_2,j}\}_{j\in\mathbb Z^{\geq 0}}.
$$

If true, this would give the desired countably infinite analogue of a difference matrix over the infinite cyclic group, whose additive group is the group of integers. The claim is presented as a conjectural generalization of an earlier theorem; no resolution is supplied in the given text.

382419.title: Feasible indexing conjecture for successor and ancestor sets of weakly connected DAGs
382419.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a weakly connected directed acyclic graph with $n$ nodes, and let an indexing assign the nodes the labels $1,\ldots,n$. For each node $v$, let $\mathcal S(v)$ be its successor set and let $\mathcal A(v)$ be its ancestor set:

$$
\mathcal A(v)=\\{u\in V\backslash\\{v\\}\mid \text{node }u\text{ can reach node }v\\}.
$$

Let $LO(\mathcal S(v))$ and $LO(\mathcal A(v))$ denote the associated lexicographic orders, and suppose the indexing satisfies the paper's constraint $LO(\mathcal S(v))\le LO(\mathcal S(v+1))$ for all $v\in[n-1]$.

**Feasible indexing conjecture.** There exists an indexing satisfying this successor-set ordering and, whenever two consecutive nodes have equal successor-set order,

$$
LO(\mathcal S(v))=LO(\mathcal S(v+1))\Rightarrow LO(\mathcal A(v))\le LO(\mathcal A(v+1)),\qquad \forall v\in[n-1].
$$

This strengthens the successor-set ordering to break ties using ancestor sets. The paper reports numerical verification for every weakly connected DAG with at most $7$ nodes, but gives no general construction of a feasible indexing; the conjecture remains open.
